name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
summary: A Democrat whose New Deal built federal social insurance, labor protections and financial regulation, raised top tax rates, and created public enterprises such as the TVA. He led the United States in World War II and made founding the United Nations his top postwar goal.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Listed 'the right to adequate medical care and the opportunity to achieve and enjoy good health' in his 1944 Second Bill of Rights, though no national health program was enacted. In 1941 he said 'we should widen the opportunities for adequate medical care.'

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Signed the Fair Labor Standards Act (1938), which re-established a federal minimum wage and overtime and banned child labor; called for 'the right to earn enough to provide adequate food and clothing and recreation.'

markets-allocate-better.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

public-ownership.rationale: Created the Tennessee Valley Authority (1933), a public corporation that built dams and power stations.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Signed the Revenue Act of 1935, with a 79% rate on income over $5 million, and in 1944 called for a tax law 'which will tax all unreasonable profits, both individual and corporate.'

unions-good.rationale: Signed the National Labor Relations Act (1935) and pledged to 'support collective bargaining.'

property-fundamental.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Created the Securities and Exchange Commission and signed Glass-Steagall; warned that 'Government by organized money is just as dangerous as Government by organized mob.'

cut-welfare.rationale: Created Social Security and unemployment insurance, while saying 'we prefer useful work to the pauperism of a dole.'
